lines.note: `Fanarebanare` means separate parts or pieces. The following example applies separation to the body, not merely to people living apart.

The body becomes separated into pieces. `Ientai` is anomalous if 全体 is intended; retain the visible initial provisionally and flag it rather than treating the kana hint as a satisfactory interpretation.
Portuguese explicitly says the body is in pieces or dismembered. This confirms the physical, rather than social, sense of separation in the example.
`Fanarejima` is a detached or isolated island. The compound's geographic meaning is directly confirmed by `Ilha apartada`.
`Fanareqiri` means completely separating or detaching. The completion force of `-qiri` is expressed by `de todo` below.
Complete detachment is followed by a second sense, becoming determined. Both involve reaching a decisive state rather than partial separation.
`Fanare qitta fito` is a resolute person. The Portuguese finishes determination before introducing this example.
After the determined-person gloss, `Fanare qitta xucqe` gives a religious practitioner detached from worldly things. The noun's religious meaning governs the next line.
The practitioner is detached from everything. This completes the renunciatory sense rather than describing someone physically separated from a group.
`Fanaſaqi` describes flowers blooming. The paradigm's abbreviated ending is retained; Portuguese supplies the intransitive blossoming sense.
Trees and herbs flowering extend the definition beyond a single rose. The line completes the same botanical verb.

runs.text: Peças de ſeda de Iapão tin-

lines.note: `Fanaſomeguinu` denotes pieces of Japanese silk with a specified dye color. `guinu` retains hard ギ in the cloth compound.
The cloth is dyed red. This color specification belongs to the textile definition, not the neighboring nose vocabulary.
`Fanaſugi` is the ridge of the nose, 鼻筋. Bare `gi` represents the historical ヂ series in this compound.
`Fanaſui` names a small bird that eats flowers. The gloss alone does not establish a modern species or whether nectar-feeding is intended more narrowly.
`Fanatachibana` is described as a fragrant flower. Do not substitute a modern plant identification solely from the compound's familiar syllables.

runs.text: Vaſo em que poem flores a maneira

lines.note: `Fanatate` is a vessel in which flowers are arranged. The bouquet comparison below identifies its use.
“Like a bouquet” completes the flower-vessel description. This is not another example of the verb standing or rising.
`Fanatçumi` is flower-picking. The example repeats the noun, split before the following line's `miuo`.
`Fanatçumiuo ſuru` means performing flower-picking. The split is physical and must not create a separate `miuo` word in interpretation.

runs.text: Adu. De roſto a roſto, ou

lines.note: `Fanatçuqini` is face-to-face or directly opposite. The grammatical label marks an adverb, not an object or flower name.
The encounter is face-to-face. The enlarged scan reads `yuqiuǒ`, a visibly unusual spelling where 行き会う is expected; preserve its medial letter rather than silently regularizing to `yuqiǒ`.
`Encontrarſe de roſto a roſto` confirms meeting face-to-face. This supports the intended verb while leaving its irregular printed spelling visible.
`Fanauo` is the thong of Japanese footwear, 鼻緒. It is a whole noun here, not `fana` followed by object particle `uo`.

runs.text: de Iapão que ſe encaixa entre os dedos dos pes.

lines.note: The thong fits between the toes. This physical detail confirms the sandal-part sense of the preceding compound.
This `Fanaxi` means detaching or separating. Its examples below extend the action to releasing projectiles and animals.
`Yauo fanaſu` means shooting an arrow. The basic release meaning remains visible in the Japanese object and verb.
`Teppǒuo fanaſu, l, vtçu` gives alternative verbs for firing a gun. The object is the firearm, not the person shot.
The gun gloss finishes. `Tori, qedamono` then names birds and beasts as the objects of letting go.

runs.text: Largar, ou ſoltar paſſaros, ou a-

lines.note: `uo fanaſu` completes releasing those animals. The Portuguese likewise gives freeing birds or beasts.
`a- / nimaes` completes the animal list. This short line closes the release sense before the next homograph.
This `Fanaxi` means talking or conversing. Portuguese `Praticar` is conversational here, not modern “practice” imposed on the definition.
`Nochini gozatte fanaſaxerarei` politely invites someone to come later and talk. Read the honorific and request morphology together rather than as independent dictionary forms.
“Later, and converse” completes the Portuguese invitation. It confirms the conversation homograph rather than releasing an object.
`Fanaxicaqe` here means releasing a dog upon prey. Despite the modern familiar 話しかける, the definition belongs to the release family.

runs.text: mar a caça, &c. ¶ Item, Deſparar eſpin-

lines.note: The dog takes the quarry; another sense begins with firing a gun. Both maintain the directed-release action.
A firearm or cannon completes the list. The line continues the shooting sense, not the conversational homograph.
The compiler prefers `fanachigai` to `Fanaxigai`. This expresses a lexical preference without authorizing deletion of either printed form.

runs.text: ou animal que ſe cria fora da gayola ſolto.

lines.note: A bird or animal is raised loose, outside a cage. The definition supplies the husbandry sense of the compound.
`Fanaxigaini ſuru` means keeping an animal in that free-ranging manner. The Portuguese repetition links it to the preceding definition.
Being outside the cage completes the example. The line is a continuation rather than another headword for a cage.
`Fanaxiſute` means discharging without aiming at a target. The second verb adds disposal or release rather than an intended hit.

runs.text: da, ou arco, ſem apontar a nada. ¶

lines.note: A gun or bow may be discharged without aiming. `Tebi-` starts a Japanese weapon name continued below.
`Tebi- / Yano cuſuriuo` concerns the weapon's powder charge. The printed capital at the break does not make `Yano` an independent name.

runs.text: ſem atirar de propoſito pera não ter a poluora

lines.note: The discharge is not aimed at anything, so powder will not remain loaded. `de propoſito` concerns deliberate targeting in this context.
The powder should not stay inside the gun for a long time. This completes the reason for the discharge, not an additional weapon definition.
`Fanaxite` first denotes a good, engaging speaker. This derives from the conversation sense rather than shooting.

runs.text: graça. ¶ Itẽ, Homem q̃ atira com eſpingarda.

lines.note: The second sense is a person who fires a gun. The one spelling thus covers agents from two different `fanaxi` meanings.
`Fanaxôbi` names a red flower. Its resemblance to modern plant names is not enough to force a botanical identification or change its vowel mark.
`Fanayacana` means beautiful, elegant, or splendid. The ending `-na` fits the attributive adjectival form.
`lu- / ſtroſa` completes the lustrous or splendid quality. It belongs to the same adjective, not an additional entry.
`Fanayacani` is the adverbial counterpart, “splendidly.” The Portuguese similarly uses adverbial expressions.
The adverbial gloss ends, then `Sono fitono` begins an example about that person's clothing. Keep the genitive with the next line.
`xǒzocu ichidãto fanayacani miyeta` means the attire looked especially splendid. `Yax.` is a citation label, not part of the Japanese sentence.

runs.text: O veſtido daquelle homem parecia mui galante,

lines.note: Portuguese translates the man's clothing as appearing very elegant. This confirms that clothing, not the man's behavior, is the subject.
“Brilliant” completes the description of the attire. The short line closes the literary example.
`Fanazono` is a flower garden. The Portuguese directly confirms the 花園 compound.
`Fanazzuri` is equated with `Fanaguri`, the cattle nose-ring. This repetition lets the material description be compared with f168.

runs.text: de era, ou vimes que metem pollas ventas dos

lines.note: The scan reads `de era`, ivy, matching f168's ring materials, not wax (`cera`). Withies provide the other flexible material.
The ring is placed through cattle nostrils. This completes the object definition and distinguishes it from decorative rings.
`Fanbacama` denotes a kind of short trousers or hakama. The half-length implication is supported by the Portuguese, though no exact modern garment is specified.

runs.text: Certo comer de tǒfus aſſados, & de-

lines.note: `Fanben` is a food made from roasted `tǒfus`. Do not assume the ingredients of modern はんぺん; the historical definition explicitly gives tofu.
After roasting, the tofu is cooked in `Miſô`. This completes the preparation described by the dictionary, not a modern recipe reconstruction.
`Fanberi` is the historical polite being verb はんべり. The scan supports `Gozaru`, paired with `sǒrǒ`, rather than the previous `Gozuru` reading.
“To be, to exist” completes the copular gloss. `S.` remains an editorial label rather than a Japanese syllable.

runs.text: A metade de hũa peça de ſeda fina,

lines.note: `Fanbiqi` is half a piece of fine silk. The textile measure, not a count of living creatures, governs this use of `-biqi`.
The silk is called `Qinu`. This Japanese material word is embedded in the Portuguese description.
`Fanbun` is half. Its simple gloss matches the compound illustrated earlier in the dictionary.
The scan supports `Fancai`, not `Fincai`, in the half-open/half-closed expression. `Fanbun firaqi` explicitly provides “half open.”
`fanbunua fuſagatte aru coto` supplies “the other half is closed.” The Japanese balanced structure is a useful check on the compound above.
Portuguese repeats half-open and half-closed. This confirms the contrast rather than an obscure independent `Fincai` term.
`Madara naru taqe` means mottled bamboo, supporting 斑竹. The attributive `naru` belongs to the descriptive Japanese phrase.
The bamboo has several colors. This completes the botanical appearance description without naming a modern species.
`Fandai` is a high dining table. The example begins with the same noun and continues its postposition below.
`Fandaini mucǒ, l, tçuqu` means facing or taking one's place at the table. The Portuguese gloss expresses sitting or placing oneself there.
`Fandan` concerns reasoning or deciding, compatible with 判断. `Cotouari, u` supplies the verbal explanation.
The reasoning may concern a lawsuit or dispute. The line then adds deciding or settling the matter.
The scan supports `reſoluer`, “resolve,” in the judge comparison, rather than `reſoluar`. This supplies the decision-making sense of the headword.

runs.text: A metade de hũa varzea, peça, can-

lines.note: This `Fandan` instead means half of something measured by `tan`. Fields and pieces of material show that it is a measure-related homograph.

runs.text: ga, & de outras couſas que ſe contão por Ittan,

lines.note: `Ittan` names one unit in the Japanese counting series. It belongs inside the Portuguese explanation, not a newly introduced headword.
`nitan` supplies two units, continuing the same count. The definition concerns halving objects measured in that series.

runs.text: Hum vaſo de metal em que tem agoa

lines.note: `Fandô` is a metal vessel containing water. Its tea-related use is specified below.

runs.text: pera o Chanoyu, ou outros vſos. As vezes

lines.note: The water serves `Chanoyu` or other purposes. This is a Japanese practice name embedded in Portuguese prose.

runs.text: ainda que ſeja de barro ſe diz,

lines.note: The name may also apply to an earthenware vessel. Material variation is explicitly allowed by the compiler, so “metal” is not an absolute restriction.
This `Fane` means wings. The next entry has another sense of the same spelling, not a description of feathers becoming muddy.

runs.text: Lama que ſalta por de tras nos veſtidos

lines.note: The second `Fane` is mud splashed onto clothing from behind. The source of the splash follows below.

runs.text: dos çapatos, ou alparcas de Iapão. ¶

lines.note: Japanese shoes or sandals throw up the mud. `Fa-` begins the example noun continued on the next line.
`Fanega agaru` means the splash rises. Portuguese describes the clothes being spattered, translating the result rather than matching the Japanese subject literally.

runs.text: ta lama dos çapatos por de tras.

lines.note: The mud comes from footwear behind the wearer. This completes the splash example and its physical direction.
`Fane` as a verb first means kicking. `Cubiuo` begins a separate beheading example, not a body part being kicked in the first gloss.
`Cubiuo fanuru` means cutting off the head. Another sense of the same verb begins after `Item`.

runs.text: Aleuantar algum pao, ou porta de

lines.note: The next sense is raising wood or a door. The following lines explain leaving it lifted or held aside.

runs.text: maneira que fique ſuſpenſa, & pinchada pera

lines.note: The object remains suspended and pushed to one side. This is the physical result of lifting it, not a separate adjective entry.

runs.text: hũa parte. ¶ Item. Dar paparote com o

lines.note: The sideward position completes that sense. A further finger-flicking sense then begins.

runs.text: dedo à maneira dos gafanhotos quãdo ſe ſacodẽ

lines.note: The flick is compared with grasshoppers shaking themselves. The sentence continues onto f170, where the feet and another verb are supplied.
